```h
/* SPDX-License-Identifier: GPL-2.0-or-later
 *
 * Stand-in for GL/glew.h: CCGSubSurf.c includes it, and uses it only in the
 * WITH_OPENSUBDIV code, which is not built here. */

```

`src/thirdparty/blender/shim/MEM_guardedalloc.h`:

```h
/* SPDX-License-Identifier: GPL-2.0-or-later
 *
 * Stand-in for Blender's intern/guardedalloc, for the CCGSubSurf files in the
 * folder above: the same calls, on the C library's allocator. The name string
 * Blender uses for leak reports is dropped. */
#ifndef UMK3_SHIM_MEM_GUARDEDALLOC_H
#define UMK3_SHIM_MEM_GUARDEDALLOC_H

#include <stdlib.h>

/* The game forces src/runtime/savestate.h into every file, and outside the
 * state files it maps realloc() and free() to its own -- function-like
 * macros, which CCGSubSurf's allocator fields of the same names (four
 * arguments) cannot pass through. This code frees only what it allocated
 * itself, so the C library's pair is the right one here. */
#undef malloc
#undef calloc
#undef realloc
#undef free

#define MEM_mallocN(len, str)       malloc(len)
#define MEM_callocN(len, str)       calloc(1, len)
#define MEM_reallocN(ptr, len)      realloc(ptr, len)
#define MEM_freeN(ptr)              free(ptr)

#endif

```

`src/thirdparty/blender/umk3_subsurf.c`:

```c
/* SPDX-License-Identifier: GPL-2.0-or-later
 *
 * umk3_subsurf.c -- Blender's Weld and Subdivision Surface modifiers for the
 * game's triangle meshes. See umk3_subsurf.h for the interface.
 *
 * Where each part comes from (Blender sources, GPL-2.0-or-later):
 *
 *   Weld, "All" mode, Blender 4.2.0
 *     blenlib/intern/kdtree_impl.h        BLI_kdtree_3d_new/insert/balance,
 *                                          kdtree_order, deduplicate_recursive,
 *                                          BLI_kdtree_3d_calc_duplicates_fast
 *     geometry/intern/mesh_merge_by_distance.cc
 *                                          mesh_merge_by_distance_all: the
 *                                          duplicate map with use_index_order;
 *                                          create_merged_mesh: a vertex that
 *                                          merges takes the mean of its group,
 *                                          a face left with a repeated vertex
 *                                          is removed, and of faces with the
 *                                          same vertices the first is kept
 *                                          (poly_find_doubles)
 *
 *   Subdivision Surface, Catmull-Clark, Blender 2.79b
 *     blenkernel/intern/CCGSubSurf*.c     unchanged, in this folder
 *     blenkernel/intern/subsurf_ccg.c     _getSubSurf, ss_sync_from_uv,
 *                                          ss_sync_ccg_from_derivedmesh,
 *                                          get_ss_weights, getFaceIndex,
 *                                          set_subsurf_legacy_uv (the quad
 *                                          corner order a, d, c, b)
 *     blenkernel/intern/mesh_mapping.c    BKE_mesh_uv_vert_map_create
 *     blenlib/intern/math_geom.c          cross_poly_v2
 *
 * The UV mesh is synced on its own, as Blender's subsurf does with
 * "Subdivide UVs", to tell which output vertices are shared; the UVs and
 * the per-corner data (the light) are carried with the face weights Blender
 * uses for loop custom data.
 *
 * What is not Blender: the glue -- arrays in, arrays out, vertices shared
 * between grids by their CCG element, triangles from the grid quads -- and
 * that the topology is synced once and only positions change per call. */
#include <stdint.h>
#include <stdlib.h>
#include <string.h>
#include <math.h>

#include "MEM_guardedalloc.h"
#include "BLI_utildefines.h"
#include "CCGSubSurf.h"
#include "umk3_subsurf.h"

#define SWAP(type, a, b) { type sw_ap; sw_ap = (a); (a) = (b); (b) = sw_ap; }
#define POINTER_FROM_INT(i) ((void *)(intptr_t)(i))
#define POINTER_AS_INT(p)   ((int)(intptr_t)(p))

/* BKE_mesh_mapping.h */
#define STD_UV_CONNECT_LIMIT 0.0001f

/* ======================================================= kdtree_impl.h, 3D */

#define KD_DIMS 3
#define KD_NODE_UNSET ((unsigned)-1)
#define KD_NODE_ROOT_IS_INIT ((unsigned)-2)

typedef struct KDTreeNode_head {
	unsigned left, right;
	float co[KD_DIMS];
	int index;
} KDTreeNode_head;

typedef struct KDTreeNode {
	unsigned left, right;
	float co[KD_DIMS];
	int index;
	unsigned d; /* range is only (0..KD_DIMS - 1) */
} KDTreeNode;

typedef struct KDTree {
	KDTreeNode *nodes;
	unsigned nodes_len;
	unsigned root;
	int max_node_index;
} KDTree;

static void copy_vn_vn(float v0[KD_DIMS], const float v1[KD_DIMS])
{
	for (unsigned j = 0; j < KD_DIMS; j++) {
		v0[j] = v1[j];
	}
}

static float square_f(float a)
{
	return a * a;
}

static float len_squared_vnvn(const float v0[KD_DIMS], const float v1[KD_DIMS])
{
	float d = 0.0f;
	for (unsigned j = 0; j < KD_DIMS; j++) {
		d += square_f(v0[j] - v1[j]);
	}
	return d;
}

static KDTree *kdtree_new(unsigned nodes_len_capacity)
{
	KDTree *tree;

	tree = MEM_mallocN(sizeof(KDTree), "KDTree");
	tree->nodes = MEM_mallocN(sizeof(KDTreeNode) * nodes_len_capacity, "KDTreeNode");
	tree->nodes_len = 0;
	tree->root = KD_NODE_ROOT_IS_INIT;
	tree->max_node_index = -1;
	return tree;
}

static void kdtree_free(KDTree *tree)
{
	if (tree) {
		MEM_freeN(tree->nodes);
		MEM_freeN(tree);
	}
}

static void kdtree_insert(KDTree *tree, int index, const float co[KD_DIMS])
{
	KDTreeNode *node = &tree->nodes[tree->nodes_len++];

	/* NOTE: array isn't calloc'd,
	 * need to initialize all struct members */

	node->left = node->right = KD_NODE_UNSET;
	copy_vn_vn(node->co, co);
	node->index = index;
	node->d = 0;
	tree->max_node_index = MAX2(tree->max_node_index, index);
}

static unsigned kdtree_balance(KDTreeNode *nodes, unsigned nodes_len, unsigned axis, const unsigned ofs)
{
	KDTreeNode *node;
	float co;
	unsigned left, right, median, i, j;

	if (nodes_len <= 0) {
		return KD_NODE_UNSET;
	}
	else if (nodes_len == 1) {
		return 0 + ofs;
	}

	/* Quick-sort style sorting around median. */
	left = 0;
	right = nodes_len - 1;
	median = nodes_len / 2;

	while (right > left) {
		co = nodes[right].co[axis];
		i = left - 1;
		j = right;

		while (1) {
			while (nodes[++i].co[axis] < co) { /* pass */
			}
			while (nodes[--j].co[axis] > co && j > left) { /* pass */
			}

			if (i >= j) {
				break;
			}

			SWAP(KDTreeNode_head, *(KDTreeNode_head *)&nodes[i], *(KDTreeNode_head *)&nodes[j]);
		}

		SWAP(KDTreeNode_head, *(KDTreeNode_head *)&nodes[i], *(KDTreeNode_head *)&nodes[right]);
		if (i >= median) {
			right = i - 1;
		}
		if (i <= median) {
			left = i + 1;
		}
	}

	/* Set node and sort sub-nodes. */
	node = &nodes[median];
	node->d = axis;
	axis = (axis + 1) % KD_DIMS;
	node->left = kdtree_balance(nodes, median, axis, ofs);
	node->right = kdtree_balance(
	        nodes + median + 1, (nodes_len - (median + 1)), axis, (median + 1) + ofs);

	return median + ofs;
}

static void kdtree_balance_tree(KDTree *tree)
{
	if (tree->root != KD_NODE_ROOT_IS_INIT) {
		for (unsigned i = 0; i < tree->nodes_len; i++) {
			tree->nodes[i].left = KD_NODE_UNSET;
			tree->nodes[i].right = KD_NODE_UNSET;
		}
	}

	tree->root = kdtree_balance(tree->nodes, tree->nodes_len, 0, 0);
}

/**
 * Use when we want to loop over nodes ordered by index.
 * Requires indices to be aligned with nodes.
 */
static int *kdtree_order(const KDTree *tree)
{
	const KDTreeNode *nodes = tree->nodes;
	const size_t bytes_num = sizeof(int) * (size_t)(tree->max_node_index + 1);
	int *order = MEM_mallocN(bytes_num, __func__);
	memset(order, -1, bytes_num);
	for (unsigned i = 0; i < tree->nodes_len; i++) {
		order[nodes[i].index] = (int)i;
	}
	return order;
}

struct DeDuplicateParams {
	/* Static */
	const KDTreeNode *nodes;
	float range;
	float range_sq;
	int *duplicates;
	int *duplicates_found;

	/* Per Search */
	float search_co[KD_DIMS];
	int search;
};

static void deduplicate_recursive(const struct DeDuplicateParams *p, unsigned i)
{
	const KDTreeNode *node = &p->nodes[i];
	if (p->search_co[node->d] + p->range <= node->co[node->d]) {
		if (node->left != KD_NODE_UNSET) {
			deduplicate_recursive(p, node->left);
		}
	}
	else if (p->search_co[node->d] - p->range >= node->co[node->d]) {
		if (node->right != KD_NODE_UNSET) {
			deduplicate_recursive(p, node->right);
		}
	}
	else {
		if ((p->search != node->index) && (p->duplicates[node->index] == -1)) {
			if (len_squared_vnvn(node->co, p->search_co) <= p->range_sq) {
				p->duplicates[node->index] = (int)p->search;
				*p->duplicates_found += 1;
			}
		}
		if (node->left != KD_NODE_UNSET) {
			deduplicate_recursive(p, node->left);
		}
		if (node->right != KD_NODE_UNSET) {
			deduplicate_recursive(p, node->right);
		}
	}
}

/* BLI_kdtree_3d_calc_duplicates_fast, with use_index_order as
 * mesh_merge_by_distance_all passes it (true). */
static int kdtree_calc_duplicates_fast(const KDTree *tree, const float range, int *duplicates)
{
	int found = 0;
	struct DeDuplicateParams p;

	memset(&p, 0, sizeof(p));
	p.nodes = tree->nodes;
	p.range = range;
	p.range_sq = square_f(range);
	p.duplicates = duplicates;
	p.duplicates_found = &found;

	{
		int *order = kdtree_order(tree);
		for (int i = 0; i < tree->max_node_index + 1; i++) {
			const int node_index = order[i];
			if (node_index == -1) {
				continue;
			}
			const int index = i;
			if (duplicates[index] == -1 || duplicates[index] == index) {
				p.search = index;
				copy_vn_vn(p.search_co, tree->nodes[node_index].co);
				int found_prev = found;
				deduplicate_recursive(&p, tree->root);
				if (found != found_prev) {
					/* Prevent chains of doubles. */
					duplicates[index] = index;
				}
			}
		}
		MEM_freeN(order);
	}
	return found;
}

/* ===================================================== math_geom.c, 2.79b */

static float cross_poly_v2(const float verts[][2], unsigned int nr)
{
	unsigned int a;
	float cross;
	const float *co_curr, *co_prev;

	/* The Trapezium Area Rule */
	co_prev = verts[nr - 1];
	co_curr = verts[0];
	cross = 0.0f;
	for (a = 0; a < nr; a++) {
		cross += (co_curr[0] - co_prev[0]) * (co_curr[1] + co_prev[1]);
		co_prev = co_curr;
		co_curr += 2;
	}

	return cross;
}

/* ================================================== mesh_mapping.c, 2.79b
 *
 * BKE_mesh_uv_vert_map_create for a mesh of triangles (totloop 3 for every
 * poly, loopstart = 3 * poly), selected = false, use_winding = true -- the
 * call ss_sync_from_uv makes. */

typedef struct UvMapVert {
	struct UvMapVert *next;
	unsigned int f;
	unsigned char tfindex, separate, flag;
} UvMapVert;

typedef struct UvVertMap {
	struct UvMapVert **vert;
	struct UvMapVert *buf;
} UvVertMap;

static void uv_vert_map_free(UvVertMap *vmap)
{
	if (vmap) {
		if (vmap->vert) MEM_freeN(vmap->vert);
		if (vmap->buf) MEM_freeN(vmap->buf);
		MEM_freeN(vmap);
	}
}

static UvVertMap *uv_vert_map_create(const int *loop_v, const float (*mloopuv)[2],
                                     unsigned int totpoly, unsigned int totvert,
                                     const float limit[2])
{
	UvVertMap *vmap;
	UvMapVert *buf;
	unsigned int a;
	int i, totuv, nverts;
	bool *winding;

	totuv = (int)totpoly * 3;

	if (totuv == 0)
		return NULL;

	vmap = (UvVertMap *)MEM_callocN(sizeof(*vmap), "UvVertMap");
	buf = vmap->buf = (UvMapVert *)MEM_callocN(sizeof(*vmap->buf) * (size_t)totuv, "UvMapVert");
	vmap->vert = (UvMapVert **)MEM_callocN(sizeof(*vmap->vert) * totvert, "UvMapVert*");
	winding = MEM_callocN(sizeof(*winding) * totpoly, "winding");

	if (!vmap->vert || !vmap->buf || !winding) {
		if (winding) MEM_freeN(winding);
		uv_vert_map_free(vmap);
		return NULL;
	}

	for (a = 0; a < totpoly; a++) {
		float tf_uv[3][2];

		nverts = 3;

		for (i = 0; i < nverts; i++) {
			buf->tfindex = (unsigned char)i;
			buf->f = a;
			buf->separate = 0;
			buf->next = vmap->vert[loop_v[a * 3 + i]];
			vmap->vert[loop_v[a * 3 + i]] = buf;

			tf_uv[i][0] = mloopuv[a * 3 + i][0];
			tf_uv[i][1] = mloopuv[a * 3 + i][1];

			buf++;
		}

		winding[a] = cross_poly_v2((const float (*)[2])tf_uv, (unsigned int)nverts) > 0;
	}

	/* sort individual uvs for each vert */
	for (a = 0; a < totvert; a++) {
		UvMapVert *newvlist = NULL, *vlist = vmap->vert[a];
		UvMapVert *iterv, *v, *lastv, *next;
		const float *uv, *uv2;

		while (vlist) {
			v = vlist;
			vlist = vlist->next;
			v->next = newvlist;
			newvlist = v;

			uv = mloopuv[v->f * 3 + v->tfindex];
			lastv = NULL;
			iterv = vlist;

			while (iterv) {
				next = iterv->next;

				uv2 = mloopuv[iterv->f * 3 + iterv->tfindex];

				if (fabsf(uv[0] - uv2[0]) < limit[0] && fabsf(uv[1] - uv2[1]) < limit[1] &&
				    (winding[iterv->f] == winding[v->f]))
				{
					if (lastv) lastv->next = next;
					else vlist = next;
					iterv->next = newvlist;
					newvlist = iterv;
				}
				else
					lastv = iterv;

				iterv = next;
			}

			newvlist->separate = 1;
		}

		vmap->vert[a] = newvlist;
	}

	MEM_freeN(winding);

	return vmap;
}

/* ==================================================== subsurf_ccg.c, 2.79b */

static CCGSubSurf *getSubSurf(int subdivLevels, int numLayers)
{
	CCGMeshIFC ifc;
	CCGSubSurf *ccgSS;

	/* (subdivLevels == 0) is not allowed */
	subdivLevels = MAX2(subdivLevels, 1);

	/* no aging, no arena, no normals, no mask */
	ifc.vertUserSize = ifc.edgeUserSize = ifc.faceUserSize = 8;
	ifc.numLayers = numLayers;
	ifc.vertDataSize = sizeof(float) * numLayers;
	ifc.simpleSubdiv = 0;

	ccgSS = ccgSubSurf_new(&ifc, subdivLevels, NULL, NULL);
	ccgSubSurf_setCalcVertexNormals(ccgSS, 0, 0);

	return ccgSS;
}

/* getFaceIndex, with the element bases taken from the handles this file
 * gives them (vertex i, edge i, face i, in order) instead of user data. */
typedef struct ElemBases {
	int numVerts;
	int edgeBase0;              /* numVerts */
	int *faceBase;              /* per face handle */
} ElemBases;

static int vertIndex(CCGVert *v)
{
	return POINTER_AS_INT(ccgSubSurf_getVertVertHandle(v));
}

static int edgeBase(const ElemBases *b, CCGEdge *e, int edgeSize)
{
	return b->edgeBase0 + POINTER_AS_INT(ccgSubSurf_getEdgeEdgeHandle(e)) * (edgeSize - 2);
}

static int getFaceIndex(const ElemBases *b, CCGFace *f, int S, int x, int y, int edgeSize, int gridSize)
{
	int faceBase = b->faceBase[POINTER_AS_INT(ccgSubSurf_getFaceFaceHandle(f))];
	int numVerts = ccgSubSurf_getFaceNumVerts(f);

	if (x == gridSize - 1 && y == gridSize - 1) {
		CCGVert *v = ccgSubSurf_getFaceVert(f, S);
		return vertIndex(v);
	}
	else if (x == gridSize - 1) {
		CCGVert *v = ccgSubSurf_getFaceVert(f, S);
		CCGEdge *e = ccgSubSurf_getFaceEdge(f, S);
		int eb = edgeBase(b, e, edgeSize);
		if (v == ccgSubSurf_getEdgeVert0(e)) {
			return eb + (gridSize - 1 - y) - 1;
		}
		else {
			return eb + (edgeSize - 2 - 1) - ((gridSize - 1 - y) - 1);
		}
	}
	else if (y == gridSize - 1) {
		CCGVert *v = ccgSubSurf_getFaceVert(f, S);
		CCGEdge *e = ccgSubSurf_getFaceEdge(f, (S + numVerts - 1) % numVerts);
		int eb = edgeBase(b, e, edgeSize);
		if (v == ccgSubSurf_getEdgeVert0(e)) {
			return eb + (gridSize - 1 - x) - 1;
		}
		else {
			return eb + (edgeSize - 2 - 1) - ((gridSize - 1 - x) - 1);
		}
	}
	else if (x == 0 && y == 0) {
		return faceBase;
	}
	else if (x == 0) {
		S = (S + numVerts - 1) % numVerts;
		return faceBase + 1 + (gridSize - 2) * S + (y - 1);
	}
	else if (y == 0) {
		return faceBase + 1 + (gridSize - 2) * S + (x - 1);
	}
	else {
		return faceBase + 1 + (gridSize - 2) * numVerts + S * (gridSize - 2) * (gridSize - 2) + (y - 1) * (gridSize - 2) + (x - 1);
	}
}

static void elem_bases_init(ElemBases *b, int numVerts, int numEdges, int numFaces,
                            const int *faceLen, int edgeSize, int gridSize)
{
	int i, base;

	b->numVerts = numVerts;
	b->edgeBase0 = numVerts;
	b->faceBase = MEM_mallocN(sizeof(int) * (size_t)(numFaces > 0 ? numFaces : 1), "faceBase");
	base = numVerts + numEdges * (edgeSize - 2);
	for (i = 0; i < numFaces; i++) {
		int n = faceLen ? faceLen[i] : 3;
		b->faceBase[i] = base;
		base += 1 + n * (gridSize - 2) + n * (gridSize - 2) * (gridSize - 2);
	}
}

/* get_ss_weights, for one face length (built x-major, read y-major, both as
 * Blender does -- see umk_subsurf_eval). */
static float *get_ss_weights(int gridCuts, int faceLen)
{
	int x, y, i, j;
	float *w, *w0, w1, w2, w4, fac, fac2, fx, fy;

	w0 = w = MEM_callocN(sizeof(float) * faceLen * faceLen * (gridCuts + 2) * (gridCuts + 2), "weight table alloc");
	fac = 1.0f / (float)faceLen;

	for (i = 0; i < faceLen; i++) {
		for (x = 0; x < gridCuts + 2; x++) {
			for (y = 0; y < gridCuts + 2; y++) {
				fx = 0.5f - (float)x / (float)(gridCuts + 1) / 2.0f;
				fy = 0.5f - (float)y / (float)(gridCuts + 1) / 2.0f;

				fac2 = faceLen - 4;
				w1 = (1.0f - fx) * (1.0f - fy) + (-fac2 * fx * fy * fac);
				w2 = (1.0f - fx + fac2 * fx * -fac) * (fy);
				w4 = (fx) * (1.0f - fy + -fac2 * fy * fac);

				/* these values aren't used for tri's and cause divide by zero */
				if (faceLen > 3) {
					fac2 = 1.0f - (w1 + w2 + w4);
					fac2 = fac2 / (float)(faceLen - 3);
					for (j = 0; j < faceLen; j++) {
						w[j] = fac2;
					}
				}

				w[i] = w1;
				w[(i - 1 + faceLen) % faceLen] = w2;
				w[(i + 1) % faceLen] = w4;

				w += faceLen;
			}
		}
	}

	return w0;
}

/* ================================================================== glue */

typedef struct EdgeKey {
	int v0, v1;
} EdgeKey;

struct UmkSubsurf {
	int levels;

	/* the weld */
	int nverts;                 /* input */
	int *weld_map;              /* input vertex -> welded vertex */
	int nwelded;
	int *group_count;           /* welded vertex -> members */
	int merged;

	/* the welded triangles that survive */
	int nfaces;
	int *face_src;              /* kept face -> input triangle */
	int *face_v;                /* x 3, welded vertices */
	int nedges;
	EdgeKey *edges;
	float *edge_crease;         /* per edge, Blender's crease * creaseFactor */
	float *fit_base;            /* scratch, nwelded x 3 */
	int ntris;                  /* input triangles */
	float *last_pos, *last_attr;/* the last call's input, to skip a repeat */
	int have_last, last_had_attr;

	CCGSubSurf *ss;             /* positions, 3 layers */
	CCGSubSurf *uvss;           /* UVs, 2 layers, synced once */
	float *weights;             /* get_ss_weights for triangles */
	int edgeSize, gridSize;

	/* the output, in input-face order */
	int out_nverts, out_ntris;
	int *out_ref;               /* x 4: face, S, x, y of each output vertex */
	float *out_pos, *out_uv, *out_attr;
	unsigned int *out_tri;
	float *welded_pos;          /* scratch, nwelded x 3 */
	CCGFace **faceMap;          /* positions ss, by face handle */
	CCGFace **uvFaceMap;
};

static int edge_lookup_or_add(EdgeKey **edges, int *n, int *cap, int **hash, int *hcap, int a, int b)
{
	unsigned h;
	int v0 = a < b ? a : b, v1 = a < b ? b : a;

	if (*n * 2 >= *hcap) {
		int i, ncap = *hcap ? *hcap * 2 : 1024;
		int *nh = MEM_mallocN(sizeof(int) * (size_t)ncap, "edge hash");
		for (i = 0; i < ncap; i++) nh[i] = -1;
		for (i = 0; i < *n; i++) {
			unsigned k = ((unsigned)(*edges)[i].v0 * 2654435761u ^ (unsigned)(*edges)[i].v1 * 40503u) & (unsigned)(ncap - 1);
			while (nh[k] != -1) k = (k + 1) & (unsigned)(ncap - 1);
			nh[k] = i;
		}
		if (*hash) MEM_freeN(*hash);
		*hash = nh;
		*hcap = ncap;
	}
	h = ((unsigned)v0 * 2654435761u ^ (unsigned)v1 * 40503u) & (unsigned)(*hcap - 1);
	while ((*hash)[h] != -1) {
		EdgeKey *e = &(*edges)[(*hash)[h]];
		if (e->v0 == v0 && e->v1 == v1)
			return (*hash)[h];
		h = (h + 1) & (unsigned)(*hcap - 1);
	}
	if (*n == *cap) {
		*cap = *cap ? *cap * 2 : 1024;
		*edges = MEM_reallocN(*edges, sizeof(EdgeKey) * (size_t)*cap);
	}
	(*edges)[*n].v0 = v0;
	(*edges)[*n].v1 = v1;
	(*hash)[h] = *n;
	return (*n)++;
}

/* Only the positions changed: CCG's partial sync (ccgSubSurf_initPartialSync,
 * the path Blender's own edit-mode updates take) re-sends the vertices; the
 * edges and faces of the full sync stay, so does the face map, and nothing
 * is allocated. An unchanged vertex is skipped by syncVert itself. */
static int sync_positions_partial(UmkSubsurf *s)
{
	int i;

	if (ccgSubSurf_initPartialSync(s->ss) != eCCGError_None)
		return 0;
	for (i = 0; i < s->nwelded; i++) {
		CCGVert *v;
		ccgSubSurf_syncVert(s->ss, POINTER_FROM_INT(i), s->welded_pos + i * 3, 0, &v);
	}
	return ccgSubSurf_processSync(s->ss) == eCCGError_None;
}

/* ss_sync_ccg_from_derivedmesh: the full sync, once, when the mesh is made. */
static int sync_positions(UmkSubsurf *s)
{
	CCGVertHDL fVerts[3];
	int i, j;

	ccgSubSurf_initFullSync(s->ss);

	for (i = 0; i < s->nwelded; i++) {
		CCGVert *v;
		ccgSubSurf_syncVert(s->ss, POINTER_FROM_INT(i), s->welded_pos + i * 3, 0, &v);
	}

	for (i = 0; i < s->nedges; i++) {
		CCGEdge *e;
		/* ss_sync_ccg_from_derivedmesh: me->crease * creaseFactor / 255 --
		 * the open edges at 255, the rest at 0 (see umk_subsurf_new) */
		ccgSubSurf_syncEdge(s->ss, POINTER_FROM_INT(i), POINTER_FROM_INT(s->edges[i].v0),
		                    POINTER_FROM_INT(s->edges[i].v1), s->edge_crease[i], &e);
	}

	for (i = 0; i < s->nfaces; i++) {
		CCGFace *f;

		for (j = 0; j < 3; j++) {
			fVerts[j] = POINTER_FROM_INT(s->face_v[i * 3 + j]);
		}

		if (ccgSubSurf_syncFace(s->ss, POINTER_FROM_INT(i), 3, fVerts, &f) == eCCGError_InvalidValue) {
			return 0;
		}
	}

	ccgSubSurf_processSync(s->ss);
	return 1;
}

/* ss_sync_from_uv, for triangles. Returns the number of UV vertices. */
static int sync_uvs(UmkSubsurf *s, const float (*face_uv)[2])
{
	UvVertMap *vmap;
	UvMapVert *v;
	float limit[2];
	int *loop_v, *loop_uvvert;
	int i, j, seam, nuv = 0;
	EdgeKey *edges = NULL;
	int nedges = 0, cap = 0, *hash = NULL, hcap = 0;
	float uv[3] = {0.0f, 0.0f, 0.0f}; /* only first 2 values are written into */

	limit[0] = limit[1] = STD_UV_CONNECT_LIMIT;

	loop_v = MEM_mallocN(sizeof(int) * (size_t)s->nfaces * 3, "loop_v");
	for (i = 0; i < s->nfaces * 3; i++)
		loop_v[i] = s->face_v[i];

	vmap = uv_vert_map_create(loop_v, face_uv, (unsigned)s->nfaces, (unsigned)s->nwelded, limit);
	if (!vmap) {
		MEM_freeN(loop_v);
		return 0;
	}

	/* the UV vertex of each loop: the loop that starts its "separate" run */
	loop_uvvert = MEM_mallocN(sizeof(int) * (size_t)s->nfaces * 3, "loop_uvvert");

	ccgSubSurf_initFullSync(s->uvss);

	/* create vertices */
	for (i = 0; i < s->nwelded; i++) {
		if (!vmap->vert[i])
			continue;

		for (v = vmap->vert[i]->next; v; v = v->next)
			if (v->separate)
				break;

		seam = (v != NULL);

		for (v = vmap->vert[i]; v; v = v->next) {
			if (v->separate) {
				CCGVert *ssv;
				int loopid = (int)v->f * 3 + v->tfindex;
				UvMapVert *w;

				uv[0] = face_uv[loopid][0];
				uv[1] = face_uv[loopid][1];

				ccgSubSurf_syncVert(s->uvss, POINTER_FROM_INT(nuv), uv, seam, &ssv);

				/* get_face_uv_map_vert: every loop of this run maps here */
				loop_uvvert[loopid] = nuv;
				for (w = v->next; w && !w->separate; w = w->next)
					loop_uvvert[w->f * 3 + w->tfindex] = nuv;
				nuv++;
			}
		}
	}

	/* create edges */
	for (i = 0; i < s->nfaces; i++) {
		int jn;
		for (j = 0, jn = 2; j < 3; jn = j++) {
			int v0 = loop_uvvert[i * 3 + jn];
			int v1 = loop_uvvert[i * 3 + j];
			int before = nedges;
			int e = edge_lookup_or_add(&edges, &nedges, &cap, &hash, &hcap, v0, v1);

			if (nedges != before) {
				CCGEdge *ce;
				/* crease = ccgSubSurf_getEdgeCrease(orige): 0, no creases */
				ccgSubSurf_syncEdge(s->uvss, POINTER_FROM_INT(e), POINTER_FROM_INT(v0),
				                    POINTER_FROM_INT(v1), 0.0f, &ce);
			}
		}
	}

	/* create faces */
	for (i = 0; i < s->nfaces; i++) {
		CCGVertHDL fverts[3];
		CCGFace *f;

		for (j = 0; j < 3; j++)
			fverts[j] = POINTER_FROM_INT(loop_uvvert[i * 3 + j]);
		ccgSubSurf_syncFace(s->uvss, POINTER_FROM_INT(i), 3, fverts, &f);
	}

	uv_vert_map_free(vmap);
	ccgSubSurf_processSync(s->uvss);

	if (hash) MEM_freeN(hash);
	if (edges) MEM_freeN(edges);
	MEM_freeN(loop_uvvert);
	MEM_freeN(loop_v);
	return nuv;
}

static void face_maps(CCGSubSurf *ss, CCGFace **map)
{
	CCGFaceIterator fi;

	for (ccgSubSurf_initFaceIterator(ss, &fi); !ccgFaceIterator_isStopped(&fi); ccgFaceIterator_next(&fi)) {
		CCGFace *f = ccgFaceIterator_getCurrent(&fi);
		map[POINTER_AS_INT(ccgSubSurf_getFaceFaceHandle(f))] = f;
	}
}

/* The output vertices: one per pair (position element, UV element), found
 * through getFaceIndex on both meshes; and the triangles of every grid quad,
 * a, d, c, b as set_subsurf_legacy_uv reads them. */
static int build_output(UmkSubsurf *s, int nuv, const float (*face_uv)[2])
{
	ElemBases pb, ub;
	int gridSize = s->gridSize, edgeSize = s->edgeSize, gridFaces = gridSize - 1;
	int64_t keymax;
	int i, S, x, y, n = 0, t = 0, cap, hcap;
	int64_t *hkey;
	int *hval, *idx;

	elem_bases_init(&pb, s->nwelded, s->nedges, s->nfaces, NULL, edgeSize, gridSize);
	elem_bases_init(&ub, nuv, ccgSubSurf_getNumEdges(s->uvss), s->nfaces, NULL, edgeSize, gridSize);
	keymax = (int64_t)ub.faceBase[0] + (int64_t)s->nfaces * (1 + 3 * (gridSize - 2) + 3 * (gridSize - 2) * (gridSize - 2)) + 1;

	cap = s->nfaces * 3 * gridSize * gridSize;
	hcap = 1;
	while (hcap < cap * 2) hcap <<= 1;
	hkey = MEM_mallocN(sizeof(int64_t) * (size_t)hcap, "out key");
	hval = MEM_mallocN(sizeof(int) * (size_t)hcap, "out val");
	for (i = 0; i < hcap; i++) hkey[i] = -1;

	s->out_ref = MEM_mallocN(sizeof(int) * 4 * (size_t)cap, "out_ref");
	s->out_tri = MEM_mallocN(sizeof(unsigned int) * 6 * (size_t)s->nfaces * 3 * gridFaces * gridFaces, "out_tri");
	idx = MEM_mallocN(sizeof(int) * (size_t)gridSize * gridSize, "grid idx");

	for (i = 0; i < s->nfaces; i++) {
		CCGFace *f = s->faceMap[i], *uf = s->uvFaceMap[i];

		for (S = 0; S < 3; S++) {
			for (y = 0; y < gridSize; y++) {
				for (x = 0; x < gridSize; x++) {
					int64_t key = (int64_t)getFaceIndex(&pb, f, S, x, y, edgeSize, gridSize) * keymax
					            + getFaceIndex(&ub, uf, S, x, y, edgeSize, gridSize);
					unsigned h = (unsigned)((uint64_t)key * 0x9E3779B97F4A7C15ull >> 32) & (unsigned)(hcap - 1);

					while (hkey[h] != -1 && hkey[h] != key)
						h = (h + 1) & (unsigned)(hcap - 1);
					if (hkey[h] == -1) {
						hkey[h] = key;
						hval[h] = n;
						s->out_ref[n * 4 + 0] = i;
						s->out_ref[n * 4 + 1] = S;
						s->out_ref[n * 4 + 2] = x;
						s->out_ref[n * 4 + 3] = y;
						n++;
					}
					idx[y * gridSize + x] = hval[h];
				}
			}

			for (y = 0; y < gridFaces; y++) {
				for (x = 0; x < gridFaces; x++) {
					unsigned a = (unsigned)idx[(y + 0) * gridSize + x + 0];
					unsigned b = (unsigned)idx[(y + 0) * gridSize + x + 1];
					unsigned c = (unsigned)idx[(y + 1) * gridSize + x + 1];
					unsigned d = (unsigned)idx[(y + 1) * gridSize + x + 0];

					s->out_tri[t++] = a; s->out_tri[t++] = d; s->out_tri[t++] = c;
					s->out_tri[t++] = a; s->out_tri[t++] = c; s->out_tri[t++] = b;
				}
			}
		}
	}

	s->out_nverts = n;
	s->out_ntris = t / 3;
	s->out_pos = MEM_mallocN(sizeof(float) * 3 * (size_t)n, "out_pos");
	s->out_uv = MEM_mallocN(sizeof(float) * 2 * (size_t)n, "out_uv");
	s->out_attr = MEM_callocN(sizeof(float) * (size_t)n, "out_attr");

	/* The UVs do not change: worked out once. Port, not Blender 2.79: the
	 * subdivided UV mesh moves the rim of a UV island like any boundary, and
	 * where the rim bends inwards it moves out of the island onto other
	 * parts of the texture (a dark wedge on Jax, Sektor, Kitana...). The UV
	 * mesh still decides which output vertices are shared; each UV is the
	 * face's own corner UVs mixed with the loop weights, so it stays inside
	 * the face's UV triangle (Blender 2.91+ "UV Smooth: None"). */
	for (i = 0; i < n; i++) {
		const int *r = s->out_ref + i * 4;
		const float *w = s->weights + ((r[1] * gridSize + r[3]) * gridSize + r[2]) * 3;
		const float (*c)[2] = face_uv + r[0] * 3;
		s->out_uv[i * 2 + 0] = w[0] * c[0][0] + w[1] * c[1][0] + w[2] * c[2][0];
		s->out_uv[i * 2 + 1] = w[0] * c[0][1] + w[1] * c[1][1] + w[2] * c[2][1];
	}

	MEM_freeN(idx);
	MEM_freeN(hkey);
	MEM_freeN(hval);
	MEM_freeN(pb.faceBase);
	MEM_freeN(ub.faceBase);
	return n > 0;
}

static void weld_positions(UmkSubsurf *s, const float *pos)
{
	int i;

	memset(s->welded_pos, 0, sizeof(float) * 3 * (size_t)s->nwelded);
	for (i = 0; i < s->nverts; i++) {
		float *d = s->welded_pos + s->weld_map[i] * 3;
		d[0] += pos[i * 3 + 0];
		d[1] += pos[i * 3 + 1];
		d[2] += pos[i * 3 + 2];
	}
	/* create_merged_mesh with do_mix_vert_data: the mean of the group */
	for (i = 0; i < s->nwelded; i++) {
		float k = 1.0f / (float)s->group_count[i];
		s->welded_pos[i * 3 + 0] *= k;
		s->welded_pos[i * 3 + 1] *= k;
		s->welded_pos[i * 3 + 2] *= k;
	}
}

UmkSubsurf *umk_subsurf_new(int levels, float weld_dist,
                            int nverts, const float *pos,
                            int ntris, const unsigned short *tri,
                            const float *corner_uv)
{
	UmkSubsurf *s;
	int *dup, i, j, n;
	float (*face_uv)[2];
	int *linked_off, *linked;       /* faces by welded vertex, for doubles */
	unsigned char *dead, *in_ctx, *face_ctx;
	EdgeKey *edges = NULL;
	int nedges = 0, cap = 0, *hash = NULL, hcap = 0, nuv;

	if (levels < 1 || nverts <= 0 || ntris <= 0)
		return NULL;

	s = MEM_callocN(sizeof(*s), "UmkSubsurf");
	s->levels = levels;
	s->nverts = nverts;

	/* ---- the weld: mesh_merge_by_distance_all ---- */
	dup = MEM_mallocN(sizeof(int) * (size_t)nverts, "vert_dest_map");
	for (i = 0; i < nverts; i++)
		dup[i] = -1;                    /* OUT_OF_CONTEXT */
	if (weld_dist > 0.0f) {
		KDTree *tree = kdtree_new((unsigned)nverts);
		for (i = 0; i < nverts; i++)
			kdtree_insert(tree, i, pos + i * 3);
		kdtree_balance_tree(tree);
		s->merged = kdtree_calc_duplicates_fast(tree, weld_dist, dup);
		kdtree_free(tree);
	}

	/* surviving vertices keep their order; a merged one joins its target */
	/* in the weld's context: a vertex it merged, or merged others into
	 * (vert_dest_map != OUT_OF_CONTEXT) -- only faces touching one are
	 * looked at for doubles, as weld_poly_loop_ctx_alloc does */
	in_ctx = MEM_callocN((size_t)nverts, "in_ctx");
	for (i = 0; i < nverts; i++)
		in_ctx[i] = dup[i] != -1;

	s->weld_map = MEM_mallocN(sizeof(int) * (size_t)nverts, "weld_map");
	n = 0;
	for (i = 0; i < nverts; i++)
		if (dup[i] == -1 || dup[i] == i)
			s->weld_map[i] = n++;
	for (i = 0; i < nverts; i++)
		if (!(dup[i] == -1 || dup[i] == i))
			s->weld_map[i] = s->weld_map[dup[i]];
	s->nwelded = n;
	s->group_count = MEM_callocN(sizeof(int) * (size_t)n, "group_count");
	for (i = 0; i < nverts; i++)
		s->group_count[s->weld_map[i]]++;
	MEM_freeN(dup);

	/* ---- faces: a repeated vertex kills the face ---- */
	s->face_src = MEM_mallocN(sizeof(int) * (size_t)ntris, "face_src");
	s->face_v = MEM_mallocN(sizeof(int) * 3 * (size_t)ntris, "face_v");
	dead = MEM_callocN((size_t)ntris, "dead");
	for (i = 0; i < ntris; i++) {
		int a = s->weld_map[tri[i * 3 + 0]];
		int b = s->weld_map[tri[i * 3 + 1]];
		int c = s->weld_map[tri[i * 3 + 2]];
		if (a == b || b == c || c == a)
			dead[i] = 1;
	}

	/* ---- poly_find_doubles: of faces with the same vertices the first
	 * stays (for triangles, the same set in any order) -- among the faces in
	 * the weld's context only. A game model has faces drawn both ways
	 * (cloth: the same three corners, front and back); outside the weld
	 * they are kept, as Blender keeps them. Removing them all opened holes
	 * in the fighters (Mary). ---- */
	face_ctx = MEM_callocN((size_t)ntris, "face_ctx");
	for (i = 0; i < ntris; i++)
		face_ctx[i] = in_ctx[tri[i * 3 + 0]] || in_ctx[tri[i * 3 + 1]] || in_ctx[tri[i * 3 + 2]];
	linked_off = MEM_callocN(sizeof(int) * (size_t)(n + 1), "linked_off");
	for (i = 0; i < ntris; i++)
		if (!dead[i])
			for (j = 0; j < 3; j++)
				linked_off[s->weld_map[tri[i * 3 + j]] + 1]++;
	for (i = 0; i < n; i++)
		linked_off[i + 1] += linked_off[i];
	linked = MEM_mallocN(sizeof(int) * (size_t)(linked_off[n] > 0 ? linked_off[n] : 1), "linked");
	{
		int *fill = MEM_mallocN(sizeof(int) * (size_t)(n > 0 ? n : 1), "fill");
		memcpy(fill, linked_off, sizeof(int) * (size_t)n);
		for (i = 0; i < ntris; i++)     /* ascending face order per vertex */
			if (!dead[i])
				for (j = 0; j < 3; j++) {
					int v = s->weld_map[tri[i * 3 + j]];
					linked[fill[v]++] = i;
				}
		MEM_freeN(fill);
	}
	for (i = 0; i < ntris; i++) {
		int a, b, c, k;
		if (dead[i] || !face_ctx[i])
			continue;
		a = s->weld_map[tri[i * 3 + 0]];
		b = s->weld_map[tri[i * 3 + 1]];
		c = s->weld_map[tri[i * 3 + 2]];
		for (k = linked_off[a]; k < linked_off[a + 1]; k++) {
			int g = linked[k], ga, gb, gc;
			if (g <= i || dead[g] || !face_ctx[g])
				continue;
			ga = s->weld_map[tri[g * 3 + 0]];
			gb = s->weld_map[tri[g * 3 + 1]];
			gc = s->weld_map[tri[g * 3 + 2]];
			if ((ga == a || ga == b || ga == c) && (gb == a || gb == b || gb == c)
			    && (gc == a || gc == b || gc == c))
				dead[g] = 1;
		}
	}
	MEM_freeN(linked);
	MEM_freeN(linked_off);
	MEM_freeN(face_ctx);
	MEM_freeN(in_ctx);

	face_uv = MEM_mallocN(sizeof(float) * 6 * (size_t)ntris, "face_uv");
	for (i = 0; i < ntris; i++) {
		if (dead[i])
			continue;
		for (j = 0; j < 3; j++) {
			s->face_v[s->nfaces * 3 + j] = s->weld_map[tri[i * 3 + j]];
			face_uv[s->nfaces * 3 + j][0] = corner_uv[(i * 3 + j) * 2 + 0];
			face_uv[s->nfaces * 3 + j][1] = corner_uv[(i * 3 + j) * 2 + 1];
		}
		s->face_src[s->nfaces++] = i;
	}
	MEM_freeN(dead);

	if (s->nfaces == 0) {
		MEM_freeN(face_uv);
		umk_subsurf_free(s);
		return NULL;
	}

	/* the mesh's edges, in first-seen order */
	for (i = 0; i < s->nfaces; i++)
		for (j = 0; j < 3; j++)
			edge_lookup_or_add(&edges, &nedges, &cap, &hash, &hcap,
			                   s->face_v[i * 3 + j], s->face_v[i * 3 + (j + 1) % 3]);
	if (hash) MEM_freeN(hash);
	s->edges = edges;
	s->nedges = nedges;

	/* Port, not Blender's choice of data: an edge with one face -- the rim
	 * of a piece that sits over another, Kano's eye plate, a helmet part --
	 * gets crease 1.0 (255), Blender's own way to keep an edge where it is.
	 * Without it Catmull-Clark pulls the rim in and what is under the piece
	 * shows through (Mary: Kano, Sektor). creaseFactor is the level, as in
	 * ss_sync_ccg_from_derivedmesh. */
	{
		int *uses = MEM_callocN(sizeof(int) * (size_t)(nedges > 0 ? nedges : 1), "edge uses");
		int *eh = NULL, ecap = 0, ehcap = 0, en = nedges;
		EdgeKey *ek = MEM_mallocN(sizeof(EdgeKey) * (size_t)(nedges > 0 ? nedges : 1), "edge copy");

		memcpy(ek, edges, sizeof(EdgeKey) * (size_t)nedges);
		ecap = nedges;
		en = 0;
		for (i = 0; i < s->nfaces; i++)
			for (j = 0; j < 3; j++)
				uses[edge_lookup_or_add(&ek, &en, &ecap, &eh, &ehcap,
				                        s->face_v[i * 3 + j], s->face_v[i * 3 + (j + 1) % 3])]++;
		s->edge_crease = MEM_mallocN(sizeof(float) * (size_t)(nedges > 0 ? nedges : 1), "edge_crease");
		for (i = 0; i < nedges; i++)
			s->edge_crease[i] = uses[i] == 1 ? (float)levels : 0.0f;
		if (eh) MEM_freeN(eh);
		MEM_freeN(ek);
		MEM_freeN(uses);
	}
	s->fit_base = MEM_mallocN(sizeof(float) * 3 * (size_t)(s->nwelded > 0 ? s->nwelded : 1), "fit_base");
	s->ntris = ntris;
	s->last_pos = MEM_mallocN(sizeof(float) * 3 * (size_t)nverts, "last_pos");
	s->last_attr = MEM_mallocN(sizeof(float) * 3 * (size_t)ntris, "last_attr");

	/* ---- the two subdivision surfaces ---- */
	s->ss = getSubSurf(levels, 3);
	s->uvss = getSubSurf(levels, 2);
	s->edgeSize = ccgSubSurf_getEdgeSize(s->ss);
	s->gridSize = ccgSubSurf_getGridSize(s->ss);
	s->weights = get_ss_weights(s->gridSize - 2, 3);
	s->welded_pos = MEM_mallocN(sizeof(float) * 3 * (size_t)s->nwelded, "welded_pos");
	s->faceMap = MEM_callocN(sizeof(CCGFace *) * (size_t)s->nfaces, "facemap");
	s->uvFaceMap = MEM_callocN(sizeof(CCGFace *) * (size_t)s->nfaces, "facemapuv");

	weld_positions(s, pos);
	nuv = sync_uvs(s, (const float (*)[2])face_uv);
	if (nuv == 0 || !sync_positions(s)) {
		MEM_freeN(face_uv);
		umk_subsurf_free(s);
		return NULL;
	}
	face_maps(s->ss, s->faceMap);
	face_maps(s->uvss, s->uvFaceMap);
	for (i = 0; i < s->nfaces; i++)
		if (!s->faceMap[i] || !s->uvFaceMap[i]) {
			MEM_freeN(face_uv);
			umk_subsurf_free(s);
			return NULL;
		}

	i = build_output(s, nuv, (const float (*)[2])face_uv);
	MEM_freeN(face_uv);
	if (!i) {
		umk_subsurf_free(s);
		return NULL;
	}
	return s;
}

int umk_subsurf_eval(UmkSubsurf *s, const float *pos, const float *corner_attr)
{
	int i, j;
	const int gs = s->gridSize;

	/* the same pose as last time (a pause, a held frame): nothing to do */
	if (s->have_last && memcmp(s->last_pos, pos, sizeof(float) * 3 * (size_t)s->nverts) == 0
	    && (corner_attr == NULL) == (s->last_had_attr == 0)
	    && (corner_attr == NULL || memcmp(s->last_attr, corner_attr, sizeof(float) * 3 * (size_t)s->ntris) == 0))
		return 1;

	weld_positions(s, pos);
	if (!sync_positions_partial(s))
		return 0;

	/* Port, not Blender: Catmull-Clark shrinks a closed piece, and where
	 * two pieces of a fighter overlap (Jax's head in his neck, Sektor's
	 * helmet) the shrink opens a gap. One correction pass: each control
	 * point moved by how far its subdivided self fell short of it, and the
	 * surface subdivided again -- the same CCG, so the result still passes
	 * (nearly) through the model's own vertices. */
	memcpy(s->fit_base, s->welded_pos, sizeof(float) * 3 * (size_t)s->nwelded);
	for (i = 0; i < s->nwelded; i++) {
		CCGVert *v = ccgSubSurf_getVert(s->ss, POINTER_FROM_INT(i));
		const float *lim;

		if (v == NULL)
			continue;
		lim = ccgSubSurf_getVertData(s->ss, v);
		for (j = 0; j < 3; j++)
			s->welded_pos[i * 3 + j] = s->fit_base[i * 3 + j] * 2.0f - lim[j];
	}
	if (!sync_positions_partial(s))
		return 0;

	memcpy(s->last_pos, pos, sizeof(float) * 3 * (size_t)s->nverts);
	s->last_had_attr = corner_attr != NULL;
	if (corner_attr)
		memcpy(s->last_attr, corner_attr, sizeof(float) * 3 * (size_t)s->ntris);
	s->have_last = 1;

	for (i = 0; i < s->out_nverts; i++) {
		const int *r = s->out_ref + i * 4;
		const float *co = ccgSubSurf_getFaceGridData(s->ss, s->faceMap[r[0]], r[1], r[2], r[3]);

		s->out_pos[i * 3 + 0] = co[0];
		s->out_pos[i * 3 + 1] = co[1];
		s->out_pos[i * 3 + 2] = co[2];

		if (corner_attr) {
			/* read as subsurf_ccg.c reads it for loop data:
			 * w + S * numVerts * g2_wid * g2_wid + (y * g2_wid + x) * numVerts */
			const float *w = s->weights + ((r[1] * gs + r[3]) * gs + r[2]) * 3;
			const float *a = corner_attr + s->face_src[r[0]] * 3;
			float v = 0.0f;
			for (j = 0; j < 3; j++)
				v += w[j] * a[j];
			s->out_attr[i] = v;
		}
	}
	return 1;
}

int umk_subsurf_num_verts(const UmkSubsurf *s) { return s->out_nverts; }
const float *umk_subsurf_pos(const UmkSubsurf *s) { return s->out_pos; }
const float *umk_subsurf_uv(const UmkSubsurf *s) { return s->out_uv; }
const float *umk_subsurf_attr(const UmkSubsurf *s) { return s->out_attr; }
int umk_subsurf_num_tris(const UmkSubsurf *s) { return s->out_ntris; }
const unsigned int *umk_subsurf_tris(const UmkSubsurf *s) { return s->out_tri; }
int umk_subsurf_welded(const UmkSubsurf *s) { return s->merged; }

void umk_subsurf_free(UmkSubsurf *s)
{
	if (!s)
		return;
	if (s->ss) ccgSubSurf_free(s->ss);
	if (s->uvss) ccgSubSurf_free(s->uvss);
	if (s->weld_map) MEM_freeN(s->weld_map);
	if (s->group_count) MEM_freeN(s->group_count);
	if (s->face_src) MEM_freeN(s->face_src);
	if (s->face_v) MEM_freeN(s->face_v);
	if (s->edges) MEM_freeN(s->edges);
	if (s->edge_crease) MEM_freeN(s->edge_crease);
	if (s->fit_base) MEM_freeN(s->fit_base);
	if (s->last_pos) MEM_freeN(s->last_pos);
	if (s->last_attr) MEM_freeN(s->last_attr);
	if (s->weights) MEM_freeN(s->weights);
	if (s->out_ref) MEM_freeN(s->out_ref);
	if (s->out_pos) MEM_freeN(s->out_pos);
	if (s->out_uv) MEM_freeN(s->out_uv);
	if (s->out_attr) MEM_freeN(s->out_attr);
	if (s->out_tri) MEM_freeN(s->out_tri);
	if (s->welded_pos) MEM_freeN(s->welded_pos);
	if (s->faceMap) MEM_freeN(s->faceMap);
	if (s->uvFaceMap) MEM_freeN(s->uvFaceMap);
	MEM_freeN(s);
}
```

```h
/* SPDX-License-Identifier: GPL-2.0-or-later
 *
 * umk3_subsurf -- Blender's Weld and Subdivision Surface (Catmull-Clark)
 * modifiers, for a triangle mesh with one UV per triangle corner: the shape
 * the game's skinned fighters have (docs/formats/SKIN-FORMAT.md section 10).
 *
 * Built from Blender's own code, see umk3_subsurf.c for which part comes
 * from where. Plain C, no game or platform dependency: the game links it,
 * and the launcher's model viewer runs the same file as WebAssembly. */
#ifndef UMK3_SUBSURF_H
#define UMK3_SUBSURF_H

#ifdef __cplusplus
extern "C" {
#endif

typedef struct UmkSubsurf UmkSubsurf;

/* Blender's Weld modifier default, 0.001 m. The game's models are in
 * centimetres (a fighter is about 180 units tall), so 0.1 units. */
#define UMK_WELD_DISTANCE_CM 0.1f

/* The topology, fixed for the mesh's life:
 *   levels       subdivision levels, 1 or more (Blender's "Levels Viewport")
 *   weld_dist    merge distance, in the units of `pos`; 0 = no weld
 *   pos          nverts x 3 floats: the positions the weld is measured on
 *   tri          ntris x 3 vertex indices
 *   corner_uv    ntris x 3 x 2 floats, one UV per triangle corner
 * Returns NULL when the mesh has no triangle left to subdivide. */
UmkSubsurf *umk_subsurf_new(int levels, float weld_dist,
                            int nverts, const float *pos,
                            int ntris, const unsigned short *tri,
                            const float *corner_uv);

/* One evaluation: nverts x 3 positions, and optionally one float per
 * triangle corner (ntris x 3, e.g. the light value) that is carried the way
 * Blender carries loop data through a subdivision. 0 on failure. */
int umk_subsurf_eval(UmkSubsurf *s, const float *pos, const float *corner_attr);

/* The result of the last evaluation. Vertices are unique per position and
 * UV; triangles keep the winding of the face they came from. */
int                 umk_subsurf_num_verts(const UmkSubsurf *s);
const float        *umk_subsurf_pos(const UmkSubsurf *s);    /* x 3 */
const float        *umk_subsurf_uv(const UmkSubsurf *s);     /* x 2 */
const float        *umk_subsurf_attr(const UmkSubsurf *s);   /* x 1 */
int                 umk_subsurf_num_tris(const UmkSubsurf *s);
const unsigned int *umk_subsurf_tris(const UmkSubsurf *s);   /* x 3 */

/* How many vertices the weld merged, for the log. */
int umk_subsurf_welded(const UmkSubsurf *s);

void umk_subsurf_free(UmkSubsurf *s);

#ifdef __cplusplus
}
#endif

#endif
```

`tests/gl_trace.c`:

```c
/*
 * gl_trace.c -- the two faces of the recorder. See gl_trace.h for the argument.
 *
 * The clean side calls plain `glScalef(x, y, z)`; the oracle calls
 * `stub_auto_glScalef(ctx)` and the three floats arrive as raw words in r0-r3
 * because the ABI is soft-float. Both land in the same record shape, so the
 * comparison never has to know which side produced it.
 *
 * None of the GL entry points this engine uses takes more than four arguments,
 * so r0-r3 is the whole story and no stack reading is needed here.
 */
#include "gl_trace.h"
#include "arm_runtime.h"

#include <stdio.h>
#include <stdlib.h>
#include <string.h>

glt_log  glt_clean;
glt_log  glt_oracle;
glt_log *glt_active = &glt_clean;

void glt_reset(void)
{
    glt_clean.n = glt_clean.overflow = 0;
    glt_oracle.n = glt_oracle.overflow = 0;
}

void glt_select(glt_log *dst) { glt_active = dst; }

static uint32_t f2u(float f) { uint32_t u; memcpy(&u, &f, 4); return u; }

static glt_rec *push(const char *fn, int nargs)
{
    glt_log *L = glt_active;
    glt_rec *r;
    if (L->n >= GLT_MAX_CALLS) { L->overflow++; return NULL; }
    r = &L->rec[L->n++];
    memset(r, 0, sizeof(*r));
    r->fn = fn;
    r->nargs = nargs;
    return r;
}

static void set(glt_rec *r, int i, uint32_t v, int kind)
{
    if (r == NULL || i < 0 || i > 3) return;
    /* A GLT_PTR is recorded as NULLNESS on both sides. The clean side passes a
     * host pointer and the oracle a guest address, so the raw values can never
     * agree -- recording them verbatim on one side and a 0/1 on the other
     * manufactured a divergence for every array pointer in every draw. The
     * comparison has to be symmetric or it is not a comparison. */
    r->arg[i] = (kind == GLT_PTR) ? (v != 0u) : v;
    r->kind[i] = (uint8_t)kind;
}

/* A matrix argument: copy the sixteen floats so the POINTED-AT value is what
 * gets compared, not the pointer.
 *
 * Two entry points on purpose. An earlier single function took the address as
 * a uint32_t for both sides, which TRUNCATED the clean side's 64-bit host
 * pointer and then dereferenced the result -- a segfault, not a divergence,
 * and it cost a debugging round. A guest address is four bytes and a host
 * pointer is eight; one parameter cannot be both. */
static void set_mat_host(glt_rec *r, int i, const float *p)
{
    int k;
    if (r == NULL) return;
    r->arg[i] = (p != NULL);
    r->kind[i] = GLT_MAT4;
    if (p == NULL) return;
    for (k = 0; k < 16; k++) r->mat[k] = p[k];
}

static void set_mat_guest(glt_rec *r, int i, uint32_t p)
{
    int k;
    if (r == NULL) return;
    r->arg[i] = (p != 0u);
    r->kind[i] = GLT_MAT4;
    if (p == 0u) return;
    for (k = 0; k < 16; k++) {
        uint32_t bits = MEM_LD32(p + 4u * (uint32_t)k);
        memcpy(&r->mat[k], &bits, 4);
    }
}


/* ===================================================================== */
/* clean side -- the prototypes lime.h declares                           */
/* ===================================================================== */

void glPushMatrix(void)   { push("glPushMatrix", 0); }
void glPopMatrix(void)    { push("glPopMatrix", 0); }
void glLoadIdentity(void) { push("glLoadIdentity", 0); }
void glFlush(void)        { push("glFlush", 0); }

void glEnable(unsigned c)             { set(push("glEnable", 1), 0, c, GLT_SCALAR); }
void glDisable(unsigned c)            { set(push("glDisable", 1), 0, c, GLT_SCALAR); }
void glEnableClientState(unsigned a)  { set(push("glEnableClientState", 1), 0, a, GLT_SCALAR); }
void glDisableClientState(unsigned a) { set(push("glDisableClientState", 1), 0, a, GLT_SCALAR); }
void glClientActiveTexture(unsigned u){ set(push("glClientActiveTexture", 1), 0, u, GLT_SCALAR); }
void glActiveTexture(unsigned u)      { set(push("glActiveTexture", 1), 0, u, GLT_SCALAR); }
void glMatrixMode(unsigned m)         { set(push("glMatrixMode", 1), 0, m, GLT_SCALAR); }
void glShadeModel(unsigned m)         { set(push("glShadeModel", 1), 0, m, GLT_SCALAR); }
void glCullFace(unsigned m)           { set(push("glCullFace", 1), 0, m, GLT_SCALAR); }
void glDepthMask(int f)               { set(push("glDepthMask", 1), 0, (uint32_t)f, GLT_SCALAR); }

void glBindTexture(unsigned t, unsigned n)
{
    glt_rec *r = push("glBindTexture", 2);
    set(r, 0, t, GLT_SCALAR); set(r, 1, n, GLT_SCALAR);
}

void glBlendFunc(unsigned s, unsigned d)
{
    glt_rec *r = push("glBlendFunc", 2);
    set(r, 0, s, GLT_SCALAR); set(r, 1, d, GLT_SCALAR);
}

void glAlphaFunc(unsigned f, float ref)
{
    glt_rec *r = push("glAlphaFunc", 2);
    set(r, 0, f, GLT_SCALAR); set(r, 1, f2u(ref), GLT_SCALAR);
}

void glTexEnvf(unsigned t, unsigned p, float v)
{
    glt_rec *r = push("glTexEnvf", 3);
    set(r, 0, t, GLT_SCALAR); set(r, 1, p, GLT_SCALAR); set(r, 2, f2u(v), GLT_SCALAR);
}

void glScalef(float x, float y, float z)
{
    glt_rec *r = push("glScalef", 3);
    set(r, 0, f2u(x), GLT_SCALAR); set(r, 1, f2u(y), GLT_SCALAR); set(r, 2, f2u(z), GLT_SCALAR);
}

void glTranslatef(float x, float y, float z)
{
    glt_rec *r = push("glTranslatef", 3);
    set(r, 0, f2u(x), GLT_SCALAR); set(r, 1, f2u(y), GLT_SCALAR); set(r, 2, f2u(z), GLT_SCALAR);
}

void glColor4f(float a, float b, float c, float d)
{
    glt_rec *r = push("glColor4f", 4);
    set(r, 0, f2u(a), GLT_SCALAR); set(r, 1, f2u(b), GLT_SCALAR);
    set(r, 2, f2u(c), GLT_SCALAR); set(r, 3, f2u(d), GLT_SCALAR);
}

void glMultMatrixf(const float *m)
{
    set_mat_host(push("glMultMatrixf", 1), 0, m);
}

static void ptr_call(const char *fn, int size, unsigned type, int stride, const void *p)
{
    glt_rec *r = push(fn, 4);
    set(r, 0, (uint32_t)size, GLT_SCALAR);
    set(r, 1, type, GLT_SCALAR);
    set(r, 2, (uint32_t)stride, GLT_SCALAR);
    set(r, 3, (p != NULL), GLT_PTR);
}

void glVertexPointer(int s, unsigned t, int st, const void *p)   { ptr_call("glVertexPointer", s, t, st, p); }
void glTexCoordPointer(int s, unsigned t, int st, const void *p) { ptr_call("glTexCoordPointer", s, t, st, p); }
void glColorPointer(int s, unsigned t, int st, const void *p)    { ptr_call("glColorPointer", s, t, st, p); }

void glDrawElements(unsigned mode, int count, unsigned type, const void *idx)
{
    glt_rec *r = push("glDrawElements", 4);
    set(r, 0, mode, GLT_SCALAR);
    set(r, 1, (uint32_t)count, GLT_SCALAR);
    set(r, 2, type, GLT_SCALAR);
    set(r, 3, (idx != NULL), GLT_PTR);
}

void glDeleteTextures(int n, const unsigned *t)
{
    glt_rec *r = push("glDeleteTextures", 2);
    set(r, 0, (uint32_t)n, GLT_SCALAR);
    set(r, 1, (t != NULL), GLT_PTR);
}


/* ===================================================================== */
/* oracle side -- the same calls, arriving as a register file             */
/* ===================================================================== */

#define R(n) (ctx->r[n])

#define GL0(name) \
    void stub_auto_##name(arm_ctx *ctx) { (void)ctx; push(#name, 0); }

#define GL1(name, k0) \
    void stub_auto_##name(arm_ctx *ctx) { set(push(#name, 1), 0, R(0), k0); }

#define GL2(name, k0, k1) \
    void stub_auto_##name(arm_ctx *ctx) { \
        glt_rec *r = push(#name, 2); \
        set(r, 0, R(0), k0); set(r, 1, R(1), k1); }

#define GL3(name, k0, k1, k2) \
    void stub_auto_##name(arm_ctx *ctx) { \
        glt_rec *r = push(#name, 3); \
        set(r, 0, R(0), k0); set(r, 1, R(1), k1); set(r, 2, R(2), k2); }

#define GL4(name, k0, k1, k2, k3) \
    void stub_auto_##name(arm_ctx *ctx) { \
        glt_rec *r = push(#name, 4); \
        set(r, 0, R(0), k0); set(r, 1, R(1), k1); \
        set(r, 2, R(2), k2); set(r, 3, R(3), k3); }

GL0(glPushMatrix)

/* Integer modulo. Real code, not a stub: the frame walk depends on it and a
 * wrong remainder would move every key lookup. */
void stub_auto_modsi3(arm_ctx *ctx)
{
    int32_t a = (int32_t)R(0), b = (int32_t)R(1);
    ctx->r[0] = (uint32_t)(b == 0 ? 0 : a % b);
}

/* Neither should be reached by the scene renderers. If one is, say so rather
 * than continuing quietly with a wrong trace. */
void stub_auto_objc_msgSend(arm_ctx *ctx)
{
    arm_unimplemented("stub_auto_objc_msgSend", 0u,
                      "objc_msgSend reached from a scene renderer");
    (void)ctx;
}

void stub_auto_sprintf_chk(arm_ctx *ctx)
{
    if (R(0)) MEM_ST8(R(0), 0u);        /* leave a valid empty string */
    ctx->r[0] = 0u;
}


/* ===================================================================== */

static int arg_eq(const glt_rec *a, const glt_rec *b, int i, int *ptr_only)
{
    if (a->kind[i] != b->kind[i]) return 0;
    if (a->kind[i] == GLT_PTR) { (*ptr_only)++; return a->arg[i] == b->arg[i]; }
    if (a->kind[i] == GLT_MAT4) {
        if (a->arg[i] != b->arg[i]) return 0;
        return a->arg[i] == 0u || memcmp(a->mat, b->mat, sizeof(a->mat)) == 0;
    }
    return a->arg[i] == b->arg[i];
}

int glt_compare(const char *what, int *ptr_only)
{
    int n = glt_clean.n < glt_oracle.n ? glt_clean.n : glt_oracle.n;
    int bad = 0, i, k, po = 0;

    if (glt_clean.overflow || glt_oracle.overflow) {
        printf("  DIVERGE %s: trace overflowed (clean=%d oracle=%d)\n",
               what, glt_clean.overflow, glt_oracle.overflow);
        bad++;
    }

    if (glt_clean.n != glt_oracle.n) {
        printf("  DIVERGE %s: %d GL calls clean vs %d oracle\n",
               what, glt_clean.n, glt_oracle.n);
        bad++;
    }

    for (i = 0; i < n; i++) {
        const glt_rec *c = &glt_clean.rec[i], *o = &glt_oracle.rec[i];
        if (strcmp(c->fn, o->fn) != 0) {
            printf("  DIVERGE %s call %d: clean=%s  oracle=%s\n", what, i, c->fn, o->fn);
            bad++;
            break;                      /* out of step: later calls are noise */
        }
        for (k = 0; k < c->nargs; k++) {
            if (!arg_eq(c, o, k, &po)) {
                printf("  DIVERGE %s call %d %s arg%d: clean=0x%08x  oracle=0x%08x\n",
                       what, i, c->fn, k, c->arg[k], o->arg[k]);
                bad++;
            }
        }
    }

    if (bad && getenv("GLT_DUMP")) {
        glt_dump(&glt_clean,  "clean",  64);
        glt_dump(&glt_oracle, "oracle", 64);
    }

    if (ptr_only) *ptr_only += po;
    return bad;
}

void glt_dump(const glt_log *log, const char *label, int limit)
{
    int i, k;
    printf("  --- %s: %d calls ---\n", label, log->n);
    for (i = 0; i < log->n && i < limit; i++) {
        const glt_rec *r = &log->rec[i];
        printf("    %3d  %-22s", i, r->fn);
        for (k = 0; k < r->nargs; k++) printf(" 0x%08x", r->arg[k]);
        printf("\n");
    }
}
```

`tests/gl_trace.h`:

```h
/*
 * gl_trace.h -- record the GL call stream from both sides and compare them.
 *
 * ## Why this exists
 *
 * docs/ENCARGO.md said closing RenderScene.cpp needed "pairing each GL enum
 * with the call that consumes it", and that doing so "means tracking register
 * liveness, not reading more literals". That is true of STATIC analysis: the
 * compiler interleaves the loads, so a `GL_VERTEX_ARRAY` sitting directly
 * before a `glClientActiveTexture` belongs to some later call and reading it
 * in place gets it wrong.
 *
 * But the oracle does not read the code, it RUNS it. recomp.py emits every
 * import as `stub_auto_glXxx(arm_ctx *ctx)`, handing us the full register file
 * at the instant of the call. Whatever value actually reaches r0 is simply
 * there. No liveness analysis is required -- the pairing is measured, not
 * inferred, and it is measured from the shipped instruction sequence.
 *
 * That is the same move that settled the debug-window stride: where one
 * decoding of the bytes is blind, the other sometimes is not.
 *
 * ## What is compared, and how honestly
 *
 * Each argument carries a kind, because not all of them can be compared:
 *
 *   GLT_SCALAR  enums, counts, sizes, strides, booleans, and floats by their
 *               BIT PATTERN. Compared exactly. This is the part that answers
 *               the pairing question.
 *
 *   GLT_MAT4    a `const float *` to sixteen floats. The pointer values differ
 *               (guest address vs host pointer) so the POINTED-AT MATRIX is
 *               compared instead, bit for bit. This is the strongest check
 *               here -- it is the actual transform handed to GL.
 *
 *   GLT_PTR     a pointer whose length is not known from the call alone
 *               (vertex and texcoord arrays). Compared only as null vs
 *               non-null, and that limit is reported in the summary rather
 *               than hidden. A divergence in the DATA behind these pointers
 *               would not be caught here.
 *
 * Order matters: the traces are compared call by call, so a missing, extra or
 * reordered GL call fails.
 */
#ifndef UMK3_GL_TRACE_H
#define UMK3_GL_TRACE_H

#include <stdint.h>

#define GLT_MAX_CALLS 4096

enum { GLT_SCALAR = 0, GLT_PTR = 1, GLT_MAT4 = 2 };

typedef struct {
    const char *fn;
    int         nargs;
    uint32_t    arg[4];
    uint8_t     kind[4];
    float       mat[16];        /* filled when a kind is GLT_MAT4 */
} glt_rec;

typedef struct {
    glt_rec rec[GLT_MAX_CALLS];
    int     n;
    int     overflow;
} glt_log;

/* Which log the next recorded call lands in. The clean C calls plain glXxx();
 * the oracle calls stub_auto_glXxx(). Both funnel here. */
extern glt_log *glt_active;
extern glt_log  glt_clean;
extern glt_log  glt_oracle;

void glt_reset(void);
void glt_select(glt_log *dst);

/* Compare the two logs. Prints every divergence. Returns the number found, and
 * reports through *ptr_only how many arguments could only be checked for
 * nullness, so a clean result never overstates itself. */
int  glt_compare(const char *what, int *ptr_only);

/* A one-line dump, for reading a call stream by eye when it does diverge. */
void glt_dump(const glt_log *log, const char *label, int limit);

/* GL entry points this recorder defines that lime.h does not declare, because
 * the clean engine never calls them directly -- they arrive from the iOS layer
 * that a test has to supply for itself. */
void glBlendFunc(unsigned sfactor, unsigned dfactor);
void glAlphaFunc(unsigned func, float ref);
void glDeleteTextures(int n, const unsigned *textures);
void glFlush(void);

#endif /* UMK3_GL_TRACE_H */

```

`tests/lime_platform_trace.c`:

```c
/*
 * lime_platform_trace.c -- the platform boundary for GL-stream tests.
 *
 * The clean engine calls a handful of symbols that live in `lime/iphone/lime.m`
 * -- the iOS layer this project rewrites rather than decompiles. For a test
 * that compares CALL STREAMS they cannot be no-ops: the oracle's copies issue
 * real GL calls, so a silent host stub shows up as a missing call and gets
 * blamed on whatever function was under test.
 *
 * These are implemented from what the ORACLE was measured to do, one function
 * at a time with `build/probe`:
 *
 *      limeEnableDepthWrites            -> glDepthMask(1)
 *      limeDisableDepthWrites           -> glDepthMask(0)
 *      limeDisableAlphaBlending         -> glDisable(0x0BE2)
 *      limeEnableAlphaBlending_Basic    -> glBlendFunc(0x0302, 0x0303), glEnable(0x0BE2)
 *      limeEnableAlphaBlending_Additive -> glBlendFunc(0x0302, 0x0001), glEnable(0x0BE2)
 *
 * 0x0BE2 is GL_BLEND, 0x0302 GL_SRC_ALPHA, 0x0303 GL_ONE_MINUS_SRC_ALPHA and
 * 0x0001 GL_ONE -- which confirms from behaviour what docs/ENCARGO.md had only
 * asserted: the additive path really is SRC_ALPHA/ONE and the basic path really
 * is the order-dependent one.
 *
 * Deliberately NOT `runtime/lime_platform.c`. That file's GL entries are
 * no-ops by design, which is right for tests comparing loaders and maths and
 * useless for one comparing a call stream. It also defines its own glXxx, so
 * linking both would collide with tests/gl_trace.c.
 */
#include "gl_trace.h"
#include "../src/decomp/lime/lime.h"

#include <stdio.h>
#include <stdlib.h>
#include <string.h>

#define GL_BLEND_                0x0BE2u
#define GL_SRC_ALPHA_            0x0302u
#define GL_ONE_MINUS_SRC_ALPHA_  0x0303u
#define GL_ONE_                  0x0001u

void limeEnableDepthWrites(void)    { glDepthMask(1); }
void limeDisableDepthWrites(void)   { glDepthMask(0); }
void limeDisableAlphaBlending(void) { glDisable(GL_BLEND_); }

void limeEnableAlphaBlending_Basic(void)
{
    glBlendFunc(GL_SRC_ALPHA_, GL_ONE_MINUS_SRC_ALPHA_);
    glEnable(GL_BLEND_);
}

void limeEnableAlphaBlending_Additive(void)
{
    glBlendFunc(GL_SRC_ALPHA_, GL_ONE_);
    glEnable(GL_BLEND_);
}

/* Host memory and files. Real but minimal -- the draw paths load nothing, and
 * these exist because other functions in the same translation units are linked
 * in and have to resolve. */
void  *limeMalloc(const char *tag, size_t n) { (void)tag; return calloc(1, n ? n : 1); }
void   limeFree(void *p) { free(p); }
size_t limeFileSize(const char *path) { (void)path; return 0; }
void  *limeLoadFile(const char *path) { (void)path; return NULL; }

/* None of these should be reached by a draw. Abort rather than return quietly:
 * a silent stub drops a call from one side only, and the divergence then gets
 * attributed to the wrong code. */
static void must_not_call(const char *who)
{
    printf("  FATAL: %s reached from a draw path\n", who);
    exit(3);
}

TEXTURE *limeLoadTexture(const char *p, int a, int b)
{ (void)p; (void)a; (void)b; must_not_call("limeLoadTexture"); return NULL; }

void limeDeleteTexture(TEXTURE *t) { (void)t; must_not_call("limeDeleteTexture"); }

void limeDrawSprite(TEXTURE *page, float x, float y, float w, float h,
                    float u0, float v0, float u1, float v1)
{ (void)page; (void)x; (void)y; (void)w; (void)h;
  (void)u0; (void)v0; (void)u1; (void)v1; must_not_call("limeDrawSprite"); }

void limeDrawRotSpriteFromTopLeft(TEXTURE *page, float x, float y,
                                  float w, float h, float u0, float v0,
                                  float u1, float v1, float angle)
{ (void)page; (void)x; (void)y; (void)w; (void)h;
  (void)u0; (void)v0; (void)u1; (void)v1; (void)angle;
  must_not_call("limeDrawRotSpriteFromTopLeft"); }

```

`tests/lime_unused_stubs.c`:

```c
/*
 * lime_unused_stubs.c -- what test_skinning_armv7_diff links against and
 * never calls: the skin and bone loaders in RenderSkinned.c reach the file and
 * texture layer, and the oracle reaches the same two texture calls. Anything
 * here that runs is a test bug, so each one says so and stops.
 */
#include "arm_runtime.h"
#include "../src/decomp/lime/lime.h"

#include <stdio.h>
#include <stdlib.h>

static void never(const char *what)
{
    fprintf(stderr, "lime_unused_stubs: %s called\n", what);
    abort();
}

void *limeMalloc(const char *tag, size_t bytes) { (void)tag; (void)bytes; never("limeMalloc"); return NULL; }
void  limeFree(void *p) { (void)p; never("limeFree"); }
void *limeLoadFile(const char *path) { (void)path; never("limeLoadFile"); return NULL; }
TEXTURE *limeLoadTexture(const char *path, int a, int b) { (void)path; (void)a; (void)b; never("limeLoadTexture"); return NULL; }
void  limeDeleteTexture(TEXTURE *t) { (void)t; never("limeDeleteTexture"); }

void func_000670a0_limeLoadTexture(arm_ctx *ctx) { (void)ctx; never("oracle limeLoadTexture"); }
void func_000673cc_limeDeleteTexture(arm_ctx *ctx) { (void)ctx; never("oracle limeDeleteTexture"); }

/* RenderMesh.c's loaders and debug cube, linked by the draw test. */
size_t limeFileSize(const char *path) { (void)path; never("limeFileSize"); return 0; }
SCENEINFO *LIME_LoadScene(const char *path, int a, const char *tex, int b) { (void)path; (void)a; (void)tex; (void)b; never("LIME_LoadScene"); return NULL; }
void func_0005f0ac_LIME_LoadScene(arm_ctx *ctx) { (void)ctx; never("oracle LIME_LoadScene"); }
```

`tests/rgl_test.c`:

```c
/*
 * rgl_test.c -- the three renderers against the same fixed-function calls.
 *
 * Not the game: a hidden 256x256 window, the GL 1.1 calls the game makes
 * (glClear, glOrtho, quads with and without a texture, blending, the alpha
 * test, depth, culling, glReadPixels, and the framebuffer objects of the 3D
 * resolution with multisampling, resolved and scaled onto the window) and
 * the pixels read back, checked against what OpenGL 1.1 defines. Run with
 * the renderer as argument: opengl, vulkan or d3d12.
 *
 *     zig cc -o rgl_test.exe tests/rgl_test.c src/runtime/render/rgl_*.c
 *            -Isrc/runtime -Isrc/runtime/platform/vulkan-include
 *            -lopengl32 -lgdi32 -luser32
 */
#include <stdio.h>
#include <stdlib.h>
#include <string.h>
#include "platform/gl.h"
#include "render/rgl.h"

#define W 256
#define H 256

static HWND g_wnd;

void plat_size(int *w, int *h) { *w = W; *h = H; }

static int g_fail;

static void expect(const char *what, int x, int y, int r, int g, int b)
{
    unsigned char p[4];
    glReadPixels(x, y, 1, 1, GL_RGBA, GL_UNSIGNED_BYTE, p);
    if (abs(p[0] - r) > 3 || abs(p[1] - g) > 3 || abs(p[2] - b) > 3) {
        printf("  FAIL %-34s at %3d,%3d: %3d %3d %3d, want %3d %3d %3d\n", what, x, y, p[0], p[1], p[2], r, g, b);
        g_fail++;
    } else
        printf("  ok   %-34s at %3d,%3d: %3d %3d %3d\n", what, x, y, p[0], p[1], p[2]);
}

static void quad(float x0, float y0, float x1, float y1, float z)
{
    glBegin(GL_QUADS);
    glTexCoord2f(0, 0); glVertex2f(x0, y0);
    glTexCoord2f(1, 0); glVertex2f(x1, y0);
    glTexCoord2f(1, 1); glVertex2f(x1, y1);
    glTexCoord2f(0, 1); glVertex2f(x0, y1);
    glEnd();
    (void)z;
}

/* a quad at depth z, through arrays (the game's meshes come that way) */
static void quad_z(float x0, float y0, float x1, float y1, float z, int ccw)
{
    float v[12] = { x0, y0, z, x1, y0, z, x1, y1, z, x0, y1, z };
    unsigned short i_ccw[6] = { 0, 1, 2, 0, 2, 3 }, i_cw[6] = { 0, 2, 1, 0, 3, 2 };
    glEnableClientState(GL_VERTEX_ARRAY);
    glVertexPointer(3, GL_FLOAT, 0, v);
    glDrawElements(GL_TRIANGLES, 6, GL_UNSIGNED_SHORT, ccw ? i_ccw : i_cw);
    glDisableClientState(GL_VERTEX_ARRAY);
}

typedef void (__stdcall *gen_t)(GLsizei, GLuint *);
typedef void (__stdcall *bind_t)(GLenum, GLuint);
typedef void (__stdcall *store_t)(GLenum, GLenum, GLsizei, GLsizei);
typedef void (__stdcall *storems_t)(GLenum, GLsizei, GLenum, GLsizei, GLsizei);
typedef void (__stdcall *att_t)(GLenum, GLenum, GLenum, GLuint);
typedef GLenum (__stdcall *stat_t)(GLenum);
typedef void (__stdcall *blit_t)(GLint, GLint, GLint, GLint, GLint, GLint, GLint, GLint, GLbitfield, GLenum);

static void *proc(const char *n)
{
    if (rgl_renderer != RGL_OPENGL)
        return rgl_proc(n);
    return (void *)wglGetProcAddress(n);
}

static void frame(void)
{
    if (rgl_renderer != RGL_OPENGL)
        rgl_present();
}

int main(int argc, char **argv)
{
    WNDCLASSA wc;
    HDC dc;
    GLuint tex;
    static const unsigned char texel[16] = { 255, 0, 0, 255, 0, 255, 0, 255, 0, 0, 255, 255, 255, 255, 255, 255 };

    rgl_renderer = rgl_parse(argc > 1 ? argv[1] : "opengl");
    memset(&wc, 0, sizeof wc);
    wc.lpfnWndProc = DefWindowProcA;
    wc.hInstance = GetModuleHandleA(NULL);
    wc.lpszClassName = "rgltest";
    wc.style = CS_OWNDC;
    RegisterClassA(&wc);
    {
        RECT r = { 0, 0, W, H };
        AdjustWindowRect(&r, WS_OVERLAPPEDWINDOW, FALSE);
        g_wnd = CreateWindowA("rgltest", "rgl test", WS_OVERLAPPEDWINDOW, 0, 0, r.right - r.left,
                              r.bottom - r.top, NULL, NULL, wc.hInstance, NULL);
    }
    dc = GetDC(g_wnd);
    if (rgl_renderer == RGL_OPENGL || !rgl_open(g_wnd, W, H)) {
        PIXELFORMATDESCRIPTOR pfd;
        memset(&pfd, 0, sizeof pfd);
        pfd.nSize = sizeof pfd;
        pfd.nVersion = 1;
        pfd.dwFlags = PFD_DRAW_TO_WINDOW | PFD_SUPPORT_OPENGL | PFD_DOUBLEBUFFER;
        pfd.cColorBits = 32;
        pfd.cDepthBits = 24;
        SetPixelFormat(dc, ChoosePixelFormat(dc, &pfd), &pfd);
        wglMakeCurrent(dc, wglCreateContext(dc));
        rgl_renderer = RGL_OPENGL;
    }
    printf("%s: %s\n", rgl_label(rgl_renderer), (const char *)glGetString(GL_RENDERER));

    /* 1. clear */
    glViewport(0, 0, W, H);
    glClearColor(0.2f, 0.4f, 0.6f, 1.0f);
    glClear(GL_COLOR_BUFFER_BIT | GL_DEPTH_BUFFER_BIT);
    expect("clear", 128, 128, 51, 102, 153);

    /* 2. an untextured quad, left half, in a 0..W x 0..H space (y up) */
    glMatrixMode(GL_PROJECTION);
    glLoadIdentity();
    glOrtho(0, W, 0, H, -1, 1);
    glMatrixMode(GL_MODELVIEW);
    glLoadIdentity();
    glDisable(GL_TEXTURE_2D);
    glColor4f(1, 0, 0, 1);
    quad(0, 0, 128, 256, 0);
    expect("red quad, left", 32, 128, 255, 0, 0);
    expect("right still clear", 200, 128, 51, 102, 153);

    /* 3. a 2x2 texture over the right half: t=0 is the bottom */
    glGenTextures(1, &tex);
    glBindTexture(GL_TEXTURE_2D, tex);
    glTexParameteri(GL_TEXTURE_2D, GL_TEXTURE_MIN_FILTER, GL_NEAREST);
    glTexParameteri(GL_TEXTURE_2D, GL_TEXTURE_MAG_FILTER, GL_NEAREST);
    glTexImage2D(GL_TEXTURE_2D, 0, GL_RGBA, 2, 2, 0, GL_RGBA, GL_UNSIGNED_BYTE, texel);
    glEnable(GL_TEXTURE_2D);
    glTexEnvf(GL_TEXTURE_ENV, GL_TEXTURE_ENV_MODE, (float)GL_MODULATE);
    glColor4f(1, 1, 1, 1);
    quad(128, 0, 256, 256, 0);
    expect("texel 0 (red), bottom left", 150, 30, 255, 0, 0);
    expect("texel 1 (green), bottom right", 230, 30, 0, 255, 0);
    expect("texel 2 (blue), top left", 150, 230, 0, 0, 255);
    expect("texel 3 (white), top right", 230, 230, 255, 255, 255);
    glColor4f(1, 1, 0, 1);              /* MODULATE: white x yellow */
    quad(192, 128, 256, 256, 0);
    expect("modulate", 230, 230, 255, 255, 0);
    glTexEnvf(GL_TEXTURE_ENV, GL_TEXTURE_ENV_MODE, (float)GL_REPLACE);
    quad(192, 128, 256, 256, 0);
    expect("replace", 230, 230, 255, 255, 255);
    glDisable(GL_TEXTURE_2D);

    /* 4. blending */
    glEnable(GL_BLEND);
    glBlendFunc(GL_SRC_ALPHA, GL_ONE_MINUS_SRC_ALPHA);
    glColor4f(0, 1, 0, 0.5f);
    quad(0, 0, 64, 64, 0);
    expect("half green over red", 32, 32, 128, 128, 0);
    glBlendFunc(GL_SRC_ALPHA, GL_ONE);
    glColor4f(0, 0, 1, 1);
    quad(0, 64, 64, 128, 0);
    expect("additive blue on red", 32, 96, 255, 0, 255);
    glDisable(GL_BLEND);

    /* 5. alpha test: GREATER 0.5 drops alpha 0.4 */
    glEnable(GL_ALPHA_TEST);
    glAlphaFunc(GL_GREATER, 0.5f);
    glColor4f(1, 1, 1, 0.4f);
    quad(64, 0, 128, 64, 0);
    expect("alpha 0.4 dropped", 96, 32, 255, 0, 0);
    glColor4f(1, 1, 1, 0.6f);
    quad(64, 0, 128, 64, 0);
    expect("alpha 0.6 kept", 96, 32, 255, 255, 255);
    glDisable(GL_ALPHA_TEST);

    /* 6. depth: near (z 0.5 -> -0.5 in the ortho's flip) then far */
    glEnable(GL_DEPTH_TEST);
    glColor4f(0, 1, 1, 1);
    quad_z(0, 128, 64, 192, 0.5f, 1);
    glColor4f(1, 0, 1, 1);
    quad_z(0, 128, 64, 192, -0.5f, 1);
    expect("depth: the nearer one", 32, 160, 0, 255, 255);
    glDisable(GL_DEPTH_TEST);

    /* 7. culling: back faces (clockwise) are dropped */
    glEnable(GL_CULL_FACE);
    glCullFace(GL_BACK);
    glColor4f(1, 1, 0, 1);
    quad_z(64, 128, 128, 192, 0, 0);
    expect("clockwise culled", 96, 160, 255, 0, 0);
    quad_z(64, 128, 128, 192, 0, 1);
    expect("counter-clockwise drawn", 96, 160, 255, 255, 0);
    glCullFace(GL_FRONT);
    glColor4f(0, 0, 0, 1);
    quad_z(64, 128, 128, 192, 0, 1);
    expect("front culled", 96, 160, 255, 255, 0);
    glDisable(GL_CULL_FACE);

    /* 8. scissored clear */
    glEnable(GL_SCISSOR_TEST);
    glScissor(0, 192, 32, 64);
    glClearColor(1, 1, 1, 1);
    glClear(GL_COLOR_BUFFER_BIT);
    glDisable(GL_SCISSOR_TEST);
    expect("scissor: inside", 16, 224, 255, 255, 255);
    expect("scissor: outside", 48, 224, 255, 0, 0);

    /* 9. the 3D resolution path: a 64x64 buffer, multisampled, resolved and
     * scaled onto the window's top-right quarter */
    {
        gen_t genfb = (gen_t)proc("glGenFramebuffers"), genrb = (gen_t)proc("glGenRenderbuffers");
        bind_t bindfb = (bind_t)proc("glBindFramebuffer"), bindrb = (bind_t)proc("glBindRenderbuffer");
        store_t store = (store_t)proc("glRenderbufferStorage");
        storems_t storems = (storems_t)proc("glRenderbufferStorageMultisample");
        att_t att = (att_t)proc("glFramebufferRenderbuffer");
        stat_t st = (stat_t)proc("glCheckFramebufferStatus");
        blit_t blit = (blit_t)proc("glBlitFramebuffer");
        GLuint fb[2], rb[3];

        if (!genfb || !blit) {
            printf("  FAIL no framebuffer objects\n");
            g_fail++;
        } else {
            genfb(2, fb);
            genrb(3, rb);
            bindfb(0x8D40, fb[0]);
            bindrb(0x8D41, rb[0]);
            store(0x8D41, 0x8058, 64, 64);
            att(0x8D40, 0x8CE0, 0x8D41, rb[0]);
            if (st(0x8D40) != 0x8CD5) { printf("  FAIL resolved buffer incomplete\n"); g_fail++; }
            bindfb(0x8D40, fb[1]);
            bindrb(0x8D41, rb[1]);
            storems(0x8D41, 4, 0x8058, 64, 64);
            att(0x8D40, 0x8CE0, 0x8D41, rb[1]);
            bindrb(0x8D41, rb[2]);
            storems(0x8D41, 4, 0x81A6, 64, 64);
            att(0x8D40, 0x8D00, 0x8D41, rb[2]);
            if (st(0x8D40) != 0x8CD5) { printf("  FAIL multisampled buffer incomplete\n"); g_fail++; }
            glViewport(0, 0, 64, 64);
            glClearColor(0, 0, 1, 1);
            glClear(GL_COLOR_BUFFER_BIT | GL_DEPTH_BUFFER_BIT);
            glMatrixMode(GL_PROJECTION);
            glLoadIdentity();
            glOrtho(0, 64, 0, 64, -1, 1);
            glColor4f(0, 1, 0, 1);
            quad(0, 0, 64, 32, 0);              /* green, bottom half */
            bindfb(0x8CA8, fb[1]);
            bindfb(0x8CA9, fb[0]);
            blit(0, 0, 64, 64, 0, 0, 64, 64, GL_COLOR_BUFFER_BIT, GL_NEAREST);
            bindfb(0x8D40, fb[0]);
            expect("resolved: bottom green", 32, 8, 0, 255, 0);
            expect("resolved: top blue", 32, 56, 0, 0, 255);
            bindfb(0x8CA8, fb[0]);
            bindfb(0x8CA9, 0);
            blit(0, 0, 64, 64, 128, 128, 256, 256, GL_COLOR_BUFFER_BIT, GL_LINEAR);
            bindfb(0x8D40, 0);
            glViewport(0, 0, W, H);
            expect("scaled: bottom green", 192, 140, 0, 255, 0);
            expect("scaled: top blue", 192, 240, 0, 0, 255);
            expect("outside the blit", 32, 32, 128, 128, 0);
        }
    }

    /* 10. a few frames, then again */
    {
        int i;
        for (i = 0; i < 3; i++) {
            glClearColor(i / 4.0f, 0, 0, 1);
            glClear(GL_COLOR_BUFFER_BIT);
            frame();
        }
        glClearColor(0, 0.5f, 0, 1);
        glClear(GL_COLOR_BUFFER_BIT);
        expect("after three presents", 10, 10, 0, 128, 0);
        frame();
    }

    printf("%s: %d failed\n", rgl_label(rgl_renderer), g_fail);
    if (rgl_renderer != RGL_OPENGL)
        rgl_close();
    return g_fail != 0;
}

```

`tests/sdl2-lint/SDL.h`:

```h
/*
 * SDL.h -- a LINT FIXTURE, not SDL2. Never in the build path.
 *
 * ## Why this exists
 *
 * `runtime/platform/sdl_gl.c` is the Linux backend. On a Windows machine CMake
 * never compiles it, so it sat completely unchecked: a typo in it would survive
 * every local build and only surface on somebody else's Linux box. That is the
 * same shape as the call-site scan that reported zero `glBindTexture` callers --
 * a check that cannot detect a known positive is not evidence of anything.
 *
 * So `tools/check.sh` syntax-checks that file against this header when real
 * SDL2 is absent.
 *
 * ## What a pass here does and does not prove
 *
 * PROVES  -- our own mistakes are gone: typos, undeclared variables, wrong
 *            argument COUNTS, missing returns, unused variables, bad struct
 *            member names on SDL_Event.
 *
 * DOES NOT PROVE -- that these declarations match real SDL2. They are written
 *            from the documented SDL2 API, which makes them a CLAIM, not a
 *            reading of an installed header. If one is wrong, this lint passes
 *            and the real build still fails.
 *
 * Which is why `tools/check.sh` prefers a real SDL2 whenever one is installed
 * and only falls back here, saying loudly which of the two it used. Install
 * SDL2 and the claim stops mattering.
 *
 * The constant VALUES below are placeholders chosen only to be distinct.
 * `-fsyntax-only` never looks at them. Do not copy them anywhere, and do not
 * link anything against this file -- the guard beneath makes that fail loudly.
 */
#ifndef UMK3_SDL2_LINT_FIXTURE_H
#define UMK3_SDL2_LINT_FIXTURE_H

#ifndef UMK3_SDL2_LINT
#error "tests/sdl2-lint/SDL.h is a lint fixture, not SDL2. Install SDL2 to build."
#endif

#include <stddef.h>
#include <stdint.h>

typedef uint8_t  Uint8;
typedef int16_t  Sint16;
typedef uint32_t Uint32;
typedef uint64_t Uint64;
typedef int32_t  Sint32;

typedef enum { SDL_FALSE = 0, SDL_TRUE = 1 } SDL_bool;

typedef struct SDL_Window SDL_Window;
typedef void *SDL_GLContext;

/* placeholder values -- see the header comment */
#define SDL_INIT_VIDEO            0x1u
#define SDL_WINDOWPOS_CENTERED    0x2
#define SDL_WINDOW_OPENGL         0x4u
#define SDL_WINDOW_RESIZABLE      0x8u
#define SDL_WINDOW_ALLOW_HIGHDPI  0x10u
#define SDLK_ESCAPE               0x20
#define SDLK_BACKSPACE            0x21
#define SDLK_RETURN               0x22
#define SDLK_KP_ENTER             0x23
#define SDLK_v                    0x24
#define KMOD_CTRL                 0x25

typedef enum {
    SDL_GL_RED_SIZE, SDL_GL_GREEN_SIZE, SDL_GL_BLUE_SIZE, SDL_GL_ALPHA_SIZE,
    SDL_GL_DEPTH_SIZE, SDL_GL_DOUBLEBUFFER, SDL_GL_CONTEXT_PROFILE_MASK
} SDL_GLattr;

#define SDL_GL_CONTEXT_PROFILE_COMPATIBILITY 0x0002

typedef enum { SDL_QUIT = 0x100, SDL_WINDOWEVENT = 0x200, SDL_KEYDOWN = 0x300,
               SDL_TEXTINPUT = 0x303, SDL_MOUSEWHEEL = 0x403 } SDL_EventType;
typedef enum { SDL_MOUSEWHEEL_NORMAL, SDL_MOUSEWHEEL_FLIPPED } SDL_MouseWheelDirection;
typedef enum {
    SDL_WINDOWEVENT_SIZE_CHANGED = 6,
    SDL_WINDOWEVENT_FOCUS_GAINED = 12,
```
